newsitem.title: QATAR: Committee opens talks on Qatar-Bahrain dispute.
newsitem.headline: Committee opens talks on Qatar-Bahrain dispute.

text.p: Foreign ministers of Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Oman and the United Arab Emirates met in Doha on Sunday to help improve Bahrain-Qatar ties soured by a territorial dispute.
The four men met their Qatari counterpart Sheikh Hamad bin Jassim bin Jabr al-Thani at the foreign ministry.

They were expected to fly to Bahrain later in the evening to continue separate mediation efforts after they failed to convince the two countries to agree to a memorandum of understanding during two meetings in Riyadh this month, Gulf Arab officials said.
Arab diplomats said the four-state mediation committee, set up by a Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) summit in Doha in December, might introduce some amendments to the document to narrow the gap.
Qatar and Bahrain have been locked for decades in a dispute over a cluster of islands, sandbanks and reefs in the Gulf, controlled by Manama since the 1930s, but also claimed by Doha.
Doha took the territorial dispute to the International Court of Justice at The Hague in 1991, a move opposed by Manama which insists on a regional solution.

Qatari officials told Reuters Doha was ready to sign the document to normalise ties with Manama if Bahrain agreed to abide by a 1990 agreement envisaging the adjudication of the court over their border row. The move angered Bahrain.

Ties were further strained after Bahrain accused two Qataris of spying -- which Doha denied -- and boycotted the GCC December summit in Qatar. Bahrain tried, convicted and later pardoned the two Qataris.
Qatari officials said their other demands included:
- A halt to Bahraini media campaigns against Doha -- which have eased considerably over the last weeks.

- A ban of any new construction on the disputed islands and a declaration that all past construction work is null and void. Bahrain has built a coastguard station on the Fash ad-Dibal, a coral reef mid-way between the two states, and a tourism resort on Hawar island.

- That the two countries not allow any group to use their territories to work against the security of the other and not shelter groups that undermine the security of the other. Qatar wants Bahrain to hand over several people it has accused of taking part a plot to topple the government last year. Bahrain denies any role.
